newsitem.title: GERMANY: German money rates rise on talk of Buba repo move.
newsitem.headline: German money rates rise on talk of Buba repo move.

text.p: German money market interest rates firmed on Thursday amid speculation the Bundesbank may signal higher interest rates at next week's auction for securities repurchase agreements, or repos.
The interest rate on overnight money in the interbank market rose as high as 3.15 percent, up from 3.00 to 3.10 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said the rise was caused by a fall in market liquidity as banks held on to funds in the belief the central bank may make it more expensive to obtain money next week.
"The rate rise is linked to speculation about next week's auction," one money dealer said.
Speculation has mounted that the Bundesbank may raise interest rates to stem the mark's slide against the dollar.

Frankfurt money dealers said the Bundesbank may return to variable-rate tenders for repo funds, a system in which the repo rate -- the Bundesbank's main money market rate -- is determined by the rate at which the banks bid for funds.

The move would signal the Bundesbank was sanctioning an increase in the key money market rate by allowing banks to bid the repo rate higher than the 3.00 percent it has been set at in fixed-rate repo tenders since August 1996.
The bank on Thursday denied market speculation that it would call a news conference or issue a statement on the repo in the course of the day.
Markets are now waiting for Tuesday, when the Bundesbank is due to set its weekly auction for repo funds and to announce what form the auction will take.
Some dealers said that the Bundesbank may set a combination of fixed and variable-rate repo tenders.
"There's a danger the market might overreact if the Bundesbank were just to set a variable-rate repo. It would immediately affect longer-term money rates," one dealer said.

A two-week variable-rate repo tender, set in conjunction with a four-week fixed-rate tender, would set a ceiling for money market rates and prevent banks from bidding the rate too high, dealers and analysts said.

"With just a variable-rate repo, the Bundesbank would be sounding the attack. But whatever change the Bundesbank makes to the repo, the market will interpret it that the rate cycle has turned," one dealer said.
Wednesday's surprisingly large net addition of 2.6 billion marks ($1.4 billion) at the Bundesbank's weekly repo tender had dampened expectations of a switch to a higher repo rate next week.
A smaller addition would have been interpreted as a means to keep the market short of liquidity and prepare the ground for higher rates.

But dealers on Thursday said the addition appeared to have purely been dictated by the Bundesbank's perception of how much money the market needed after bank deposits at the Bundesbank -- a measure of market liquidity -- fell sharply this week.
On Wednesday, commercial banks' deposits at the Bundesbank rose to 41.2 billion marks from 39.0 billion. The average for the month rose to 40.8 billion marks from 40.7 billion marks.
